lead: The engine check is where a charter week is most often saved or lost. Look at the engine cold, start it yourself, test it against the lines, and write down every number that will be read again at check-out.

fig.title: Engine bay, engine cold
lines: Oil: between the marks, dark, not milky
Coolant: between MIN and MAX
Belt: about 10 mm of give, no black dust
Seacock open, strainer clear
Filter bowl: clear fuel, no dark layer
Tray and saildrive well: dry
Lamps and buzzer at key-on: a lamp test
Oil alarm still on 15 s after start: stop

fig.title: It will not start
lines: Panel dark: the engine battery switch
Cranks, no fire: stop handle left out
Many tries: close the raw-water seacock,
each crank pumps water into the exhaust
Half a turn, then solid: water inside.
Do not crank again, call the base
Flat water, day one: note revs and speed
Later, same revs, less speed: fouled prop

fig.title: Fuel plan for the week
lines: Tank 160 L, keep 20 L: 140 L to use
Burn at cruising revs: about 4 L/h
140 ÷ 4 = 35 hours of motoring
Plan: 6 h a day × 6 days = 36 h = 144 L
So: a fuel stop midweek
Form says 2,290: have it corrected
Photograph the panel before you sign
Buzzer, steam at the exhaust
Throttle back, neutral, stop, let it cool
